intent: Browser discovery consumes service-authored NIP-51 bahia-contextvm-v1 relay sets for ContextVM request/reply traffic while preserving browser bootstrap fail-closed behavior and a permanent degraded fallback to bahia-browser-v1 for older deployments.
observed_behavior_before: web/src/lib/stores/discovery.svelte.js normalized bahia-browser-v1 and bahia-service-v1 relay sets but ignored bahia-contextvm-v1.
Browser encrypted ContextVM transport resolved relays from nostr.browser_relays only.
intended_behavior: Trusted service-authored bahia-contextvm-v1 relay sets are normalized into nostr.contextvm_relays.
When bahia-contextvm-v1 is missing or empty, nostr.contextvm_relays falls back to browser_relays and exposes degraded metadata rather than failing browser bootstrap.
Encrypted ContextVM capability remains gated by features.encrypted_nostr_requests plus service_pubkey and relay availability; relay presence alone does not enable encrypted transport.
Discovery remains event-driven through scoped REQ, EVENT, EOSE, CLOSED, and AUTH/CLOSED handling; no polling or timeout-based completion was added.
out_of_scope: NIP-42 AUTH implementation changes beyond preserving discovery CLOSED handling
